headline: EIA confirms crude stocks +17.4mb (wk Aug 7) vs -1.4mb forecast, largest weekly build since early 2023
gist: First run of the day, covering overnight developments. Official EIA weekly petroleum status report (week ending Aug 7) confirmed a massive +17.4 million barrel crude inventory build vs consensus of a 1.4mb draw -- the largest weekly build since early 2023, vastly exceeding Tuesday's already-bearish API estimate (9.07mb) covered in the prior day's 18:18 IST brief. Driver: exports slumped while imports jumped ~1.14 mb/d, bulk of the build on the Gulf Coast; refinery utilization stayed strong at 96.2%. WTI $82.46 (-0.97% vs prior close $83.27), below VWAP $83.13, lower quarter of day range ($81.90-84.35) -- broke below Tuesday's close overnight on the data. Demand 82.10-82.30 being defended repeatedly in the last few hours; supply 83.70-83.90 rejected repeatedly during the overnight fade. OPEC's Aug 12 report also cut 2026 global demand growth forecast to 580kbpd (4th straight cut), a separate mildly bearish data point, while IEA's report still flags a 1.8mb/d supply shortfall this quarter from the Iran conflict -- a split signal. Source: EIA/Bloomberg/Reuters/BOE Report. Sent with cards (bias board, news, WTI chart).

headline: Trump: US has "total control" of Hormuz and "will keep it"; Iran unmoved, transits at 1-week low
gist: Fresh overnight escalation not previously reported: Trump posted late Aug 12 that the US has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz, calling the naval blockade a "wall of steel" and saying "I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT!" -- notably tougher rhetoric than the prior "Pakistan close to a deal"/Oman-mediated "final stages" framing covered in earlier briefs. Iran continues asserting it controls the waterway and intends to impose a toll system; Hormuz ship transits fell to a one-week low overnight. Per Lloyd's List Intelligence, two vessels transiting the Omani alternate route have been struck since Aug 1 plus one attempted attack, confirming the elevated attack tempo is ongoing rather than isolated (consistent with, not distinct from, the already-covered Houthi/Egyptian-ship fatality story). This risk premium is currently being outweighed by the EIA inventory shock (see companion item) -- WTI/Brent both lower overnight despite the rhetoric. Source: Bloomberg/Al Jazeera/Lloyd's List Intelligence. Sent with cards (bias board, news, WTI chart).
